items.title: Bill Kirchner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2021
items.q: people like Henry Mancini and John Williams and Pete Rugolo and Johnny Mandel and others were writing scores for.

ctx.x: Well yeah, I’m more curious because I’ve been interested in how every generation has their high tech things that their entertainment is delivered through. And when we think back to, you and I are close in age and if we think back to our formative years, the high tech at that time, so what was in your household that you might have heard music from?

Well I mean aside from television, in the late 50s if you recall there was a sudden surge of jazz oriented scores for TV cop shows, like “Peter Gunn,” “Mr. Lucky,” “Johnny Staccato,” “Checkmates,” all these forgotten TV shows that people like Henry Mancini and John Williams and Pete Rugolo and Johnny Mandel and others were writing scores for.
